SemconvExceptionSignal duplicates the existing property/env resolution logic (including env var naming) instead of using ConfigPropertiesUtil.getString(...). Using the shared util would reduce duplication and keep config behavior consistent with other semconv opt-in flags (e.g., SemconvStability), and it avoids hard-coding the env var name.

The Javadoc for setExceptionEventExtractor says it is "Only used when stable exception semconv is enabled", but the current implementation is actually gated by the exception-signal opt-in (emitExceptionAsLogs()) in Instrumenter. Please update the comment to reflect the real behavior/flag so it doesn’t mislead future callers.

This shared HTTP server span assertion helper still unconditionally expects exception details to be present on spans for EXCEPTION cases (later in this method). With the new opt-in that can disable recording exceptions as span events (otel.semconv.exception.signal.opt-in=logs), these tests will fail when run under that mode. Consider gating span exception assertions on SemconvExceptionSignal.emitExceptionAsSpanEvents() (and optionally asserting the corresponding log signal when emitExceptionAsLogs() is enabled).

This shared HTTP client span assertion helper has multiple .hasException(...) expectations in error scenarios, which will break when exceptions are configured to be emitted as logs instead of span events (otel.semconv.exception.signal.opt-in=logs). To keep the test utility usable under both configurations, gate exception span-event assertions on SemconvExceptionSignal.emitExceptionAsSpanEvents() (and optionally assert emitted log records when emitExceptionAsLogs() is enabled).

`testExceptionSignalLogs` does not inherit the `collectMetadata` system property that is set for `tasks.test`, so when `otelProps.collectMetadata` is enabled this task won't collect metadata even though it sets `metadataConfig`. Consider moving `systemProperty("collectMetadata", otelProps.collectMetadata)` to `withType<Test>().configureEach { ... }`, or at least duplicating it inside this task as well.

This test task runs with `-Dotel.instrumentation.common.experimental.controller-telemetry.enabled=true` from the `withType<Test>().configureEach` block, but it overrides `metadataConfig` to only include `otel.semconv.exception.signal.opt-in=logs`. If metadata collection is enabled, the recorded `metadataConfig` will be incomplete. Consider including both properties in `metadataConfig` (comma-separated), similar to `testStableSemconv`.

`assertParentExceptionLog` filters for log records with a null/empty event name, but `Instrumenter`’s default exception-log behavior sets `eventName` to "exception" (see `Instrumenter.defaultExceptionEventExtractor`). This makes the Awaitility assertion unable to ever match the parent-span exception log when `otel.semconv.exception.signal.opt-in=logs` is enabled, causing the test to time out. Update the filter/assertion to expect event name "exception" (or at least include it) for the parent span’s exception log.

The comment references "docs/exceptions/exceptions-logs.md", but that path doesn’t exist in this repo. This makes the rationale hard to verify/maintain; consider updating the reference to an existing doc in this repository or linking to the semantic conventions proposal/URL instead.

SemconvExceptionSignal reads the opt-in flag exclusively via deprecated ConfigPropertiesUtil (system props/env vars). This means the setting won’t work when users configure instrumentation via Declarative Config / ExtendedOpenTelemetry (unlike SemconvStability, which consults DeclarativeConfigProperties first and only falls back to ConfigPropertiesUtil). Consider resolving this flag through ExtendedOpenTelemetry config (or ConfigProvider) first, with ConfigPropertiesUtil as a fallback, to keep new configuration paths consistent and future-proof.

The `satisfies(EXCEPTION_STACKTRACE, …)` lambda is currently asserting that the assertion object itself is non-null (`assertThat(stacktrace).isNotNull()`), which will always pass and does not verify the attribute value. Call `stacktrace.isNotNull()` (or stronger like `isNotBlank()`), consistent with other `satisfies` usage in this repo.

Same issue here: `assertThat(stacktrace).isNotNull()` only checks that the AssertJ assertion object is non-null, not the stacktrace attribute value. Use `stacktrace.isNotNull()` / `isNotBlank()` so this assertion actually validates the exported log record.

When `doEnd()` is invoked with a non-null `endTime` (via `startAndEnd()`), the emitted exception log currently uses the SDK's default timestamp ("now") instead of the provided end timestamp. Consider passing `endTime` into `emitExceptionLog` and setting it on the `LogRecordBuilder` so spans and exception logs remain time-consistent for explicit-timestamp instrumentations.

When exception-as-logs is enabled, an exception log is emitted for every non-null error regardless of whether the span is recording or even valid (e.g., suppressed spans or spans dropped by sampling). This can significantly increase log volume and diverges from the previous span-event behavior (recordException is a no-op for non-recording spans). Consider gating log emission on span.isRecording() and/or a valid SpanContext (or whatever suppression semantics you want) so exception logs follow the same suppression/sampling behavior as exception span events.

Same issue here: exception.getClass().getCanonicalName() can be null and may not match the value produced for exception.type. Prefer getName() when filtering/asserting EXCEPTION_TYPE to avoid NPEs and make the test robust.

Using exception.getClass().getCanonicalName() can return null (e.g., anonymous/local classes), which would throw NPE in the filter and also mismatches how exception.type is typically populated (Class#getName). Prefer getName() here (and in the subsequent assertions) to avoid null handling and better match semconv expectations.

These assertions use exception.getClass().getCanonicalName() for exception.type. canonicalName can be null and can differ from the emitted exception.type value (typically Class#getName). Switch to getName() to prevent potential NPEs and avoid false negatives for inner/anonymous exception classes.

In these log assertions, the code unconditionally expects the exception.message attribute to be present (equalTo(EXCEPTION_MESSAGE, exception.getMessage())). OTel exception semantic conventions typically omit exception.message when Throwable#getMessage() is null, which would make this assertion fail for null-message exceptions. Mirror AbstractHttpServerTest.assertExceptionLogs by asserting message only when non-null (or otherwise asserting it is absent).

This assertion requires exception.message to be present even when Throwable#getMessage() is null. Since exception.message is optional and may be omitted when null, this can lead to test failures on some exception types/JDKs. Consider asserting message only when non-null (or asserting absence when null), consistent with the server-side log assertion helper.

replies.body: The `val` naming convention applies to lambdas written directly inline as a `satisfies(AttributeKey, lambda)` argument, where the attribute key already documents what is being asserted. Here the lambdas are passed to a custom helper (`assertHandlerExceptionLog(typeAssertion, messageAssertion)`), and the descriptive `type`/`message` names document which attribute each lambda asserts — renaming both to `val` would lose that context. I clarified the review rule to exclude this case in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/4ff60272fabfe7da835f704e9a7927de50ffcb74.
